svg.title: A pick draws a window, not the canvas
svg.desc: One click renders a 19 x 19 attachment: a 13 x 13 readback window with a 3-cell halo around it, because an edge texel fits its plane from its neighbours and cleared neighbours would make a stroke pickable exactly where it is invisible. Two uniform fields carry the canvas into that window: origin says where its top-left sits, frame says which canvas the tiles were binned for.
svg.text: the yellow square, at the scale of the canvas
it is drawn on. That is the whole pick.
the attachment · PickView { x: 100, y: 250, w: 19, h: 19 }
physical ID pass · no scissor, halo included
copy_window · ids only, 8 B a texel
an edge texel fits its plane from cleared neighbours,
so a stroke is pickable exactly where it is invisible
the axis is looked up in tile (0, 0)'s list, and ink is
judged against triangles elsewhere on the screen
20 bytes a texel: ids 8 · depth 4 · metadata 8. The window costs 7 KB; the same target at canvas size would cost 32 MB.
